summary: Sarah E. Fraser works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, under teachers including Naiyun Tang, Joanna Gottfried Williams, Michael Baxandall, Kenneth J. DeWoskin, and Virginia Kane, and held posts at Northwestern University and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Sarah Harding is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpön Lama Tenpa, and held a post at Naropa University from circa 1992 to 2008.

Sarah J. Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Jacoby specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and the University of Virginia, and held academic posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Shaw is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins, later holding affiliations there with the Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies in 2013.
Saraju Rath works in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1914–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He held posts at the University of Calcutta and served as librarian at the Asiatic Society.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied civil engineering at Presidency University, Kolkata, and received instruction from Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel.

Sarat Sarma works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006), where he studied under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Saroja Bhate (born 1942) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University from circa 1993 to 2002, with her professorship there also attested in 2011.

Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as professor of history as attested in 1958, with affiliation further attested in 1987.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Voorhees College, Madras Christian College, and the universities of Madras, Calcutta, and Delhi. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as vice chancellor at Banaras Hindu University and chancellor at Delhi.
Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).
Satiranjan Sen specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University and held appointments as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satischandra Vidyabhusana (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Sarat Chandra Das and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Presidency University, Sanskrit College, Asiatic Society, and the University of Calcutta.

Satoru Harada (born 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo and held positions at Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and Kokushikan University (circa 1995–2018).

Satoru Noriyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Eshō Mikogami (attested 1996). Noriyama held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and served as a lecturer there from 2015 to 2017.

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis Oscar Gómez, and has held academic posts at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Satoshi Kono (born 1953) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.
